model: Curated (Claude, quotes verified against the PDF text)

cards.claim: In a yeast fermentation, a Raman probe focused just behind the reactor wall limits the scattering by the cells in the broth.
cards.quote: minimizing the influence of scattering due to the solid particles (cells)

cards.claim: Mid-IR penetrates only a short distance, which limits the analysis of dense or opaque samples without preparation.
cards.quote: MIR spectroscopy often suffers from low penetration depths, which limits its ability to analyze dense or opaque samples without additional preparation.

cards.claim: For in-line bioprocess monitoring a non-invasive optical probe is inserted directly into the bioreactor.
cards.quote: Generally, for in-line monitoring, a non-invasive optical probe is inserted in the bioreactor for data acquisition.

cards.claim: A mid-IR ATR probe was inserted into a 15 L fermenter through a standard DN 25 port.
cards.quote: An ATR probe was inserted into the bioreactor through a standard DN 25 port.

cards.claim: NIR spectra can be taken through the glass wall of the bioreactor – no immersion probe and a lower contamination risk.
cards.quote: Spectra were acquired through the glass wall of the bioreactor, significantly reducing contamination risks and eliminating the need for immersion probes.

cards.claim: A bypass flow cell (on-line) is used when the sensor cannot withstand the pressure or temperature in the vessel; the sample may then not represent the process exactly.
cards.quote: This method is employed when the measuring device cannot endure the harsh conditions present in the actual process vessel, such as high pressures or temperatures.

cards.claim: In-situ ATR-FTIR is limited by the absorption of the fiber optics, whereas Raman and NIR can even measure through glass or plastic.
cards.quote: Unlike in situ ATR-FTIR monitoring, which is limited by fiber optic absorption, Raman and NIR techniques can take measurements through glass or plastic media.

cards.claim: UV/Vis is a well-established in-line method for biomass, because the turbidity of a cell suspension follows the cell density.
cards.quote: It is also a well-established method for assessing biomass because cell suspension turbidity correlates well with cell.

cards.claim: Fluorescence only detects molecules with intrinsic fluorescence, which limits it to certain biomolecules.
cards.quote: fluorescence spectroscopy can only detect molecules that exhibit intrinsic fluorescence, limiting its applicability to certain types of bio-molecules.

cards.claim: Most metabolites do not fluoresce; fluorescence can follow them only indirectly through markers such as NADH or tryptophan.
cards.quote: Many metabolites do not exhibit intrinsic fluorescence, unless they contain aromatic rings or cofactors such as NADH and FAD, making direct fluorescence detection challenging

cards.claim: Raman followed glucose and ethanol in-line during a yeast fermentation (prediction error 2.8 % and 4.2 % of full scale).
cards.quote: The root mean square error of prediction (RMSEP) as a percentage of the full-scale measurement for glucose and ethanol was 2.76% and 4.19%, respectively.

cards.claim: Raman absorbs little in water, so it suits metabolite measurements in aqueous media.
cards.quote: exhibits lower absorbance for polar molecules like water, making it particularly well suited for analysis in aqueous environments

cards.claim: A mid-IR ATR probe in the fermenter tracked fructose, acetate and gluconacetan with PLS models.
cards.quote: PLS regression was utilized for the monitoring of fructose, acetate, and gluconacetan concentrations in the broth.

cards.claim: Raman offers the highest specificity for metabolites but is also the most expensive option.
cards.quote: Raman spectroscopy offers the highest specificity for metabolite detection but is also the most expensive

cards.claim: Background fluorescence, photobleaching, turbidity and pH of the sample affect fluorescence measurements.
cards.quote: Background fluorescence, photo-bleaching, sample turbidity, and sample pH are other factors that can affect the accuracy and precision of fluorescence measurements

cards.claim: Fluorescence signals react strongly to changes of pH, temperature and ionic strength in the bioreactor.
cards.quote: fluorescence signals can be highly sensitive to changes in bioreactor conditions such as pH, temperature, and ionic strength

cards.claim: Spectroscopic models need regular recalibration as equipment ages, the medium changes or the environment varies.
cards.quote: Maintaining model accuracy demands regular recalibration due to equipment aging, media composition shifts, or environmental variations

cards.claim: NIR glucose predictions became less accurate once glucose was low and no longer correlated with biomass growth.
cards.quote: for the fed-batch phase, when the glucose concentration was low and uncorrelated with biomass growth, the prediction accuracy was lower

cards.claim: NIR has limited sensitivity for compounds below about 0.1 %.
cards.quote: NIR exhibits limited sensitivity for compounds present at concentrations below 0.1 percent

cards.claim: Fluorescence is highly sensitive and can detect several components even at low concentrations.
cards.quote: offering high sensitivity and the capability to detect multiple components even at low concentrations

cards.claim: Like NIR, mid-IR absorbs strongly in water, which makes trace compounds hard to detect.
cards.quote: Akin to NIR, MIR experiences increased absorbance in aqueous solutions, leading to challenges in detecting trace compounds.
